label: fiction
title: The Alibi That Spoke
setting: The present-day fictional state of Orinth, after security officers prevented an attack on First Councillor Ilyra Senn during a public address.
charge: attempting a terrorist assassination of the head of government
elements: The accused intended to kill the fictional head of government.
The accused took an act that went beyond mere preparation.
The accused intended the attack to intimidate the public or coerce the fictional government for an ideological purpose.
hook: A live call bearing Corin Vale’s face cleared a suspicious delivery into the First Councillor’s venue. The call was a confirmed deepfake, and Corin was visibly elsewhere.

accused.human: Corin Vale is a civic-media consultant who built a career explaining synthetic images to schools and public offices.
accused.if_guilty: A conviction would imprison Corin for an attempted terrorist assassination and expose the trusted public educator as the architect of the deception.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Corin Vale designed a synthetic copy of Corin’s own face and voice, used it to authorize a delivery into the First Councillor’s venue, and prepared a public alibi for the same minute. The placed device and attempted activation went beyond preparation. Corin intended a death that would frighten the public and coerce government.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The decisive call was fake. Its face and voice cannot identify Corin, who was visibly attending a luncheon elsewhere. A media laboratory naturally contains recordings, models, drafts, and invoices. The prosecution has converted ordinary professional material into a sinister story because it cannot prove who made the call or controlled the device.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: The deepfake is not a defect in the prosecution case; it is Corin’s alibi by design. Before the call, Corin recorded its exact unusual phrases, paid for the private model, warned Jori to obey the digital double, and scheduled a public appearance. The device was placed, activation was attempted, and the ideological purpose was written plainly.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: Synthetic media can reproduce a person without consent, and Jori received immunity after giving inconsistent accounts. Corin’s studio work explains the source recordings and model invoice. The private essay is angry political writing, not an operational confession. If another person could combine those materials and send the call, reasonable doubt remains.

epilogue: Corin Vale was convicted. First Councillor Ilyra Senn completed the address from a secure location and later established an independent review of synthetic authorization in government venues. Jori Dane left public events work after accepting responsibility for bypassing inspection. Corin’s educational recordings were preserved as trial evidence because the same lessons once used to teach detection had been repurposed to manufacture an alibi.

beats.speaker: dc
beats.text: At 2:00 p.m., Jori Dane received a live call showing Corin Vale authorizing a private delivery into the address venue. A verified luncheon recording shows Corin speaking onstage elsewhere at that exact minute. The simultaneous appearances make the authorization call appear to be a frame created by another person. No visible interruption separates Corin’s luncheon remarks from that crucial minute.
beats.reveal_note: The simultaneous public appearance was real, but it was planned to make the synthetic authorization look like an external frame.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What did the protective search find before the First Councillor entered?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: A concealed destructive device had been placed within the secured address area.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Did the conduct stop at preparation?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. A remote activation command was sent, but our isolation system prevented it from reaching the device.

beats.text: What did the protective search find before the First Councillor entered? A concealed destructive device had been placed within the secured address area. Did the conduct stop at preparation? No. A remote activation command was sent, but our isolation system prevented it from reaching the device.
beats.reveal_note: Placement inside the protected area and the attempted activation were completed acts beyond planning; intervention, not abandonment, prevented the attack.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Did you recover Corin’s fingerprints or biological material from the device?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. We recovered neither Corin’s fingerprints nor Corin’s biological material from the device.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Can the activation record identify the person who sent the command?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: Not by itself. It identifies the prepared account used, not the operator’s body. Further investigation was required to connect that account to any individual.

beats.text: Did you recover Corin’s fingerprints or biological material from the device? No. We recovered neither Corin’s fingerprints nor Corin’s biological material from the device. Can the activation record identify the person who sent the command? Not by itself. It identifies the prepared account used, not the operator’s body. Further investigation was required to connect that account to any individual.
beats.reveal_note: The investigator accepted the physical-evidence gap. The prosecution still had to connect Corin through preparation, authorization, and intent.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What is your conclusion about the authorization call?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: The face and voice were synthetically generated. Corin did not physically speak those words during that call.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Does the call itself identify its creator?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. The finished file contains no reliable creator identity.

beats.text: What is your conclusion about the authorization call? The face and voice were synthetically generated. Corin did not physically speak those words during that call. Does the call itself identify its creator? No. The finished file contains no reliable creator identity.
beats.reveal_note: The expert correctly proved that the call was synthetic. That fact did not answer the separate question of who commissioned the synthetic performance.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Was this synthetic performance assembled from random public footage?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. It used recent high-quality recordings tailored to Corin’s face and voice.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What does that establish?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: The creator had access to purpose-made source material, although that fact alone does not identify the creator.

beats.text: Was this synthetic performance assembled from random public footage? No. It used recent high-quality recordings tailored to Corin’s face and voice. What does that establish? The creator had access to purpose-made source material, although that fact alone does not identify the creator.
beats.reveal_note: The defence expert exposed the call’s demanding source requirements while correctly stopping short of identifying who supplied them.

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: Corin’s studio archive contains a private session recorded two days before the attack. Corin repeats forty-seven calibration phrases, including the call’s unusual sentence, “Proceed despite my public appearance.” The project is named Second Presence. Its deletion was scheduled for seven minutes after the authorization call ended.
beats.reveal_note: The exact rare phrase, private source session, project name, and timed deletion show deliberate preparation of the synthetic alibi before the call.

beats.speaker: w3

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What did Corin tell you the evening before the address?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Corin said a digital double would call at two and that I must treat its delivery approval as genuine.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Did Corin mention the public luncheon?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Yes. Corin said being seen there was the point.

beats.text: What did Corin tell you the evening before the address? Corin said a digital double would call at two and that I must treat its delivery approval as genuine. Did Corin mention the public luncheon? Yes. Corin said being seen there was the point.
beats.reveal_note: Jori’s account describes the deepfake as a planned authorization and the luncheon as a deliberately staged alibi.

beats.speaker: w3

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: You first denied receiving any warning from Corin, correct?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Yes. I was afraid because I had bypassed the inspection hold.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: You received immunity before giving this account?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Limited immunity for my own breach, but no promise about what verdict this jury reaches.

beats.text: You first denied receiving any warning from Corin, correct? Yes. I was afraid because I had bypassed the inspection hold. You received immunity before giving this account? Limited immunity for my own breach, but no promise about what verdict this jury reaches.
beats.reveal_note: Jori had a clear reason to protect personal interests. The jury had to compare the testimony with records created before immunity was offered.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Why did your studio contain the Second Presence recordings?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: They were part of a demonstration showing how a public figure could be copied.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Did you authorize the delivery or attack?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: No. Someone reused my teaching material and made me appear responsible.

beats.text: Why did your studio contain the Second Presence recordings? They were part of a demonstration showing how a public figure could be copied. Did you authorize the delivery or attack? No. Someone reused my teaching material and made me appear responsible.
beats.reveal_note: The professional explanation was possible in isolation, but it did not explain the exact call phrase, timed deletion, advance warning, or ideological draft.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Why did your calendar say, “Double calls while I am seen,” at 2:00 p.m.?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: That described the demonstration.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Why was deletion scheduled seven minutes after the real call?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I cannot explain that timing. I did not choose it, and I did not inspect the deletion queue.

beats.text: Why did your calendar say, “Double calls while I am seen,” at 2:00 p.m.? That described the demonstration. Why was deletion scheduled seven minutes after the real call? I cannot explain that timing. I did not choose it, and I did not inspect the deletion queue.
beats.reveal_note: Corin’s demonstration claim did not explain why the private schedule and deletion were synchronized with the genuine attack authorization.

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: A private draft saved before the attack states: “Removing Senn will make the public fear elected rule. The frightened council will surrender its authority. My borrowed face will make their own evidence defend me.” The draft uses the same Second Presence project label as the source recordings.
beats.reveal_note: The pre-attack draft states the intended death, the ideological purpose of public intimidation and government coercion, and the planned synthetic alibi.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: You must decide whether Corin intended to kill the fictional head of government, acted beyond preparation, and intended public intimidation or government coercion for an ideological purpose. The confirmed deepfake does not itself prove innocence or guilt. Consider whether the prosecution proved that Corin commissioned it and joined it to the attempted attack.
beats.reveal_note: The direction separates the uncontested synthetic performance from the decisive issue: whether Corin deliberately created it as part of the attack.

twist: The call was unquestionably a deepfake, but it was not evidence of an external frame. Corin prepared the exact source phrases, instructed Jori to trust the digital double, scheduled a visible alibi, and timed the project’s deletion to the call.

jurors.label: Documentary editor
jurors.persona: Is alert to synthetic images but initially treats a confirmed fake as proof of a frame.

agree: A fake call initially looks like someone borrowed Corin’s face without permission.
pushback: Proving the face is synthetic does not prove who planned the performance.
concede: The exact private phrase and timed deletion show that Corin prepared this fake.
burden_drift: Corin works with synthetic media, so I expect Corin to explain every copied file.
burden_correct: Professional access is not guilt unless the prosecution connects it to this call.
final: The preparation records connect Corin to the deepfake beyond coincidence.

jurors.label: Security receptionist
jurors.persona: Focuses on authorization chains and understands the human consequence of bypassing a hold.

agree: Corin told Jori to honor the digital double before the call occurred.
concede: The studio records corroborate the warning without relying on Jori alone.
burden_drift: Jori broke the hold, so I am tempted to make Corin disprove Jori’s account.
burden_correct: The prosecution must prove the instruction, and the earlier records either do or do not.
final: The advance instruction and project record prove deliberate authorization.

jurors.label: Youth counsellor
jurors.persona: Insists that fear of terrorism cannot replace proof of the accused’s personal intent.

agree: The failed attack is grave, but gravity does not identify its author.
pushback: A political essay alone would not prove an attempted assassination.
concede: The draft becomes powerful when its borrowed-face plan matches the completed call.
burden_drift: The danger of the event makes an uncertain inference feel acceptable.
burden_correct: The same burden applies here: every charged element must be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
final: The matched plan, preparation, and attempted activation satisfy that burden.

jurors.label: Software auditor
jurors.persona: Tracks purpose, access, and deletion as a sequence rather than treating any file as decisive alone.

agree: A clean deepfake file cannot identify its creator by itself.
pushback: The creator question must be answered by the surrounding preparation records.
concede: The exact phrase and scheduled deletion turn access into a planned sequence.
burden_drift: Specialized access can tempt us to assume responsibility without tracing use.
burden_correct: We need the trace from Corin’s source session to this specific performance.
final: That trace is complete enough to establish Corin’s commission of the call.

jurors.label: Café owner and foreperson
jurors.persona: Keeps the room focused on the three legal elements and asks for a source beside every claim.

agree: The placement and attempted activation clearly went beyond preparation.
pushback: We still need to decide whether Corin intended the death and ideological coercion.
concede: The private draft states both purposes and matches the method actually used.
burden_drift: We are in danger of asking Corin to identify an alternative operator.
burden_correct: The judge said the prosecution must prove Corin joined the synthetic call to the attack.
final: Each element has a separate record, and those records converge on Corin.

jurors.label: Theatre usher
jurors.persona: Is strongly influenced by a convincing performance and then by evidence showing how it was staged.

agree: Seeing Corin at the luncheon while the call happened makes the frame look convincing.
pushback: A staged alibi is still a performance, even when the public appearance is real.
concede: Corin’s warning that being seen was the point changes the whole scene.
burden_drift: Because Corin understands performance, I almost expect proof that nobody copied the material.
burden_correct: The prosecution must show Corin staged this performance, not merely that Corin could.
final: The advance warning proves the public appearance was part of the deception.

jurors.label: Sound engineer
jurors.persona: Distinguishes synthetic speech from the human decisions made before and after its creation.

agree: The expert proved synthetic speech, not an innocent source.
pushback: No fingerprint in the output can erase the matching private source session.
concede: The rare sentence links Corin’s recording to the finished call with unusual precision.
burden_drift: The technical complexity makes me want Corin to explain the entire production chain.
burden_correct: We should rely on the proved links, not demand an impossible negative from Corin.
final: The source material and timing identify Corin’s deliberate preparation.

jurors.label: Compliance officer
jurors.persona: Distrusts witnesses who receive immunity but looks for records that independently corroborate them.

agree: Jori’s first denial and later immunity require caution.
pushback: An interested witness cannot carry this accusation without independent support.
concede: The prior source session and calendar note corroborate Jori on the central point.
burden_drift: Jori’s admitted breach makes me want Corin to prove Jori acted alone.
burden_correct: The prosecution must corroborate Jori, and the pre-call records are the proper test.
final: Jori is imperfect, but the independent preparation records support the account.

jurors.label: Courier dispatcher
jurors.persona: Understands delivery pressure and is prone to blaming the person who appears to control the paperwork.

agree: Jori acted because Corin had prepared Jori to trust the digital double.
pushback: A delivery bypass can involve several people, so command still needs proof.
concede: The warning before the call proves Corin controlled the authorization sequence.
burden_drift: Corin owned the model, so Corin should have to show who else used it.
burden_correct: Ownership is not enough; the prosecution must prove the specific criminal use.
final: The advance instruction proves that specific use.

jurors.label: Graduate researcher
jurors.persona: Starts undecided and changes position when separate records support one causal explanation.

agree: At first, either a frame or a self-made alibi seems possible.
pushback: The confirmed deepfake leaves the creator question open only until we examine preparation.
concede: The source phrase, calendar note, and draft all support the same planned alibi.
burden_drift: Corin’s expertise makes the innocent explanation feel like Corin’s responsibility to prove.
burden_correct: Expertise is only context; the prosecution still needs a specific connection.
final: The specific connections are too numerous and synchronized to be accidental.

jurors.label: Retired paramedic
jurors.persona: Centers the prevented human harm and requires clear proof that intervention stopped a completed attempt.

agree: The device was placed and activation was attempted before security intervened.
pushback: A prevented death still requires proof of who intended it.
concede: Corin’s draft states the intended death and the public fear it was meant to cause.
burden_drift: The avoided harm makes me impatient with any innocent explanation.
burden_correct: Prevention does not lower the burden of proving the accused’s intent.
final: The draft and completed acts prove both intent and attempt.
